To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasticizers are important for the stability and electrochemical performance of Li + polymer electrolytes.
the use of mixed plasticizer compositions in the polymer electrolyte system results in a more stable and mechanically superior electrolyte with improved electrochemical characteristics.

plasticizer mixtures of ethylene carbonate (EC) and propylene carbonate (PC) are superior to pure EC and PC in the following aspects: (1) they have higher thermal stability; (2) they have higher conductivity; (3) they display better interfacial properties between lithium metal and V 6 O 12 cathodes; and (4) they have higher lithium cycling efficiencies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new polymer electrolyte systems for ambient-temperature rechargeable Li batteries.
the development of new electrolytes for use in rechargeable batteries.
the development of a new class of polymer electrolytes based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) and lithium salts for ambient temperature lithium batteries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mixed plasticizers EC : PC in the proportion 50 : 50 are the most promising for use in Li + polymer electrolytes for ambient-temperature applications.
the use of mixed PC : EC plasticizers with the appropriate ratio of the two components is the most desirable choice for the preparation of Li + polymer electrolyte systems.
the best plasticizer composition for a Li + polymer electrolyte is a mixture of EC and PC in a ratio of 1:1 by volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best performance of the Li + polymer electrolyte was obtained with the mixed plasticizer composition of 50 : 50 EC : PC, which was also the composition that gave the highest ionic conductivity.
a plasticizer mixture of EC : PC in the proportion of 50 : 50 was found to be optimal in terms of chemical and electrochemical stability, mechanical stability and Li cycling efficiency.
the use of mixed plasticizer compositions in the preparation of Li + polymer electrolytes results in electrolytes that are more stable and more efficient in Li cycling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mixed plasticizer electrolytes can be prepared with improved thermal stability and interfacial and mechanical properties.
the use of a mixed plasticizer system in Li+ polymer electrolytes results in a material with superior electrochemical and chemical properties.
the use of mixed plasticizer compositions is a viable approach to improving the performance of ambient-temperature polymer lithium electrolytes.
